items.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.summary: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following…

items.title: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use
items.summary: Failure diagnosers for robot manipulation are increasingly vision--language models (VLMs), trained and evaluated on single-arm failures produced by perturbing a successful demonstration. items.title: When Is Additional Retrieval Worthwhile? A Cost-Aware Study of Evidence Gain and Answer Reliability in RAG
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can benefit from more sophisticated retrieval, but extra retrieval may be unnecessary for many questions and gains in evidence retrieval may not translate into faithful or correct answers. items.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
items.summary: Background and purpose: Radiotherapy planning agents based on large language models (LLMs) decide when to submit a plan or request review but are evaluated mainly by dose. This study developed OpenGray, a benchmark of planning tasks with known correct decisions. Materials and methods: OpenGray adds tasks with known an…

items.title: Tessera: Structure-Completed Evidence Units for Web Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Web retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) splits a page into fixed-size text chunks or, in recent visual pipelines, screenshot tiles, and the retrieved item serves at once as the unit of indexing, ranking, and reading. items.title: p-DCIM: A 28nm Probabilistic SRAM DCIM based Ising Machine for Near-Memory Context Selection in LLM-RAG Pipeline
items.summary: We present a fabricated SRAM DCIM Ising machine that performs set-level context selection for large language model (LLM) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). In RAG, the evidence-selection stage is increasingly delegated to repeated language-model reranking, which adds substantial energy to the inference pipelin…

items.title: SpectRAG: Weighted Chunk Graphs for Token-Budgeted Context Selection in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems ground large language models (LLMs) by retrieving external evidence and conditioning generation on the retrieved context. Although dense retrieval is effective for local semantic matching, independently ranked retrieval can return redundant passages, miss cross-chunk depend…

items.title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are extending agent-mediated commerce on the Web from shopping for consumers to operating businesses for sellers. In online-to-offline (O2O) commerce, decisions are issued through Web-based platforms but realized through costly physical execution. Evaluating such agents requires going…

items.title: TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on memory systems to leverage long-term interactions, yet existing systems typically retrieve memories based on their relevance to the current query and use them as contextual evidence. However, relevance alone does not characterize how a memory contributes to task solving: the s…

items.title: DocSkill: Skill-Integrated Agentic Reasoning for Multilingual Multi-Hop Document Question Answering
items.summary: Multilingual multi-hop document question answering (MMHop-DocQA) requires locating and integrating evidence across complex layouts, document pages, and diverse languages. Existing approaches include single-pass processing and adaptive tool use, but learning to coordinate evidence acquisition, cross-page integration, a…

items.title: Stratum: Repository Memory for Coding Agents Beyond the Context Window
items.summary: Context windows have grown a thousand-fold, yet coding agents still start every session with no memory of their past work. They re-read files, retry failed approaches, and forget root causes they established hours earlier. This is not a context-length problem but a memory-architecture problem. Our hypothesis: coding a…

items.title: Context Is a Pipeline, Not a Window: Information Attrition in LLM Agent Harnesses
items.summary: LLM agents are judged by two numbers: the size of the context window, and how often the final answer is correct. Both numbers miss a third thing: how much of a tool's output is lost before the model ever sees it. We measured this loss in a real tool-using agent. The agent finds the cause of injected faults by reading…

items.title: MarkovSim: an LLM Agent Harness with Bounded Context for Long-Horizon Computational Simulation
items.summary: Recent studies have applied large language model (LLM) agent systems to computational simulation workflows. Such workflows are long-horizon, so the information generated can exceed what an LLM can reason over at once, its context window. items.title: Learning to Remember: Advances in Memory Mechanisms for Large Language Models
items.summary: Memory has become a central mechanism for extending large language models (LLMs) beyond fixed context windows, stateless interaction, and static parametric knowledge. This survey organizes the literature around three complementary dimensions: the life cycle of memory, the storage substrate, and the system role that me…

items.title: Agent Memory as Recommendation: Recommender-System Design for Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents that serve users across many sessions must choose, for every request, the few stored memories that enter a limited context window. This choice largely decides whether the agent answers correctly, and it runs on every request at Web scale. This selection faces three challenges: a large…

items.title: CodeMeepo: A Multi-Agent Workflow for Repository-Level Code Migration and Optimization
items.summary: Repository-level code migration rewrites an entire project in a new programming language while preserving its observable behavior. items.title: Large Language Models: A Plain-Language Overview for Engineers
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are neural networks trained on huge text collections to generate text by predicting what comes next. items.title: CTXAgent - Self-Controlled Context Management of LLM Agents
items.summary: Agent harnesses keep long sessions inside the context window by compacting the history when a token threshold is crossed. Changed OpenTelemetry mcp_server.name to report the real name of fixed-URL remote MCP servers declared by plugins from the official Anthropic marketplace, instead of custom
Fixed interrupting Claude not taking effect until a timeout while an MCP server had not answered a resource read or a skill was still downloading
Fixed long hidden thinking being cut off as idle on Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS, where the endpoint sends thinking progress updates

Changed ultrathink in the interactive terminal to run its turn at xhigh effort on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 through Anthropic's API; typed while Claude is working, it raises the rest of that turn
Windows: Fixed PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks letting a tool call through when Git Bash is missing and the hook's command is only quoted strings, such as a quoted path
Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions

Fixed hooks that run in PowerShell not blocking when the hook's program exits with code 2, and on Windows PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks with "shell": "powershell" failing open when Git for Windows isn't install…
Changed the /claude-api skill to build Managed Agents subagent teams on multiagent_20261001 with dynamic workflows on by default, instead of coordinator
Fixed MCP servers showing "needs authentication" in claude -p on macOS while the login keychain was locked; they now say why, and the next run after an unlock connects without a new sign-in
Fixed MCP servers being reported as timed out, and staying failed in headless runs, when a macOS or Linux computer went to sleep while they were connecting
Fixed a turn sometimes starting without an SDK MCP server's latest tools when a background task was running
Fixed write tools on a directly configured GitHub MCP server showing a form that closed without creating anything in the desktop app's Code tab
Improved the time to the first reply in cloud sessions when one of the desktop app's MCP servers can't connect
Fixed an MCP server passed by a cloud session or by the SDK's setMcpServers being replaced later in the session by a same-named server from your own settings
Improved artifacts with several views: Claude now routes each view on the link's #name and no longer says the address bar stays the same as you switch views
Fixed artifact publishes and updates being refused for some ordinary pages, such as pages with certain minified scripts or artifacts Claude could not read first
Changed the /artifacts delete confirmation to take 1 or Enter to keep, 2 to delete, and Esc to cancel; y and n no longer answer it
[VSCode] Added a "Running start-up hooks" spinner status, with a screen reader announcement, while SessionStart or Setup hooks run
Fixed the spinner, OpenTelemetry effort values and transcripts naming a newly picked effort level during a task before the model applied it; they now show the level in force

Changed automatic model switches after a flagged message to also cover model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names; set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK=1 to turn them off
[Cloud sessions] Added an effort level to the model picker when you create or edit a routine that runs in the cloud
Changed /code-review to tell Claude to put the effort level first and use max only when asked
Improved fork subagents launched together: each is now told which launch is its own, so forks are much less likely to try to start each other's work
Fixed Claude overwriting a very large CLAUDE.md, rules file or @-included file in a subdirectory after seeing only its start; Write now asks Claude to read it all or edit in place
Fixed per-directory and paths: skills not being found after a Bash cd deeper into a git repository

Changed Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and Mantle to use the shorter system prompt for model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names and inference profile ARNs, even when they front Sonnet or Haik…

**docs:** improve the descriptions of the code execution tool and its encrypted results

**tools:** leave the tool runner's history to the caller after append_messages(), and keep the current reply out of the set_messages_params() callback
**tools:** keep running the tool runner's function tools when set_messages_params() gives tools as definitions, and stop running one it takes out of tools
**tools:** give the set_messages_params() callback of a tool runner its tools as definitions again
**tools:** keep a tool runner's betas, user_profile_id and workspace_id when set_messages_params() leaves them out
**docs:** improve the descriptions of the code execution tool and its encrypted results
**tools:** copy the messages a tool runner is created with again
**tools:** restore what the tool runner does after setMessagesParams() or pushMessages() in the loop body
**docs:** add credential expiry descriptions to the Managed Agents API reference
**docs:** improve Managed Agents memory store descriptions
**docs:** improve Managed Agents vault and credential descriptions
